These non-GAAP financial measures include: gross revenue less network fees, which includes interchange and adjustment fees; non-GAAP net income; non-GAAP EPS; free cash flow; Adjusted Free Cash Flow; earnings before interest expense, interest income, income taxes, depreciation, and amortization (“EBITDA”); Adjusted EBITDA; Adjusted EBITDA conversion rate; and Adjusted EBITDA margin. Gross revenue less network fees ("GRLNF"), including total and organic, represents a key performance metric that management uses to measure changes in the mix and value derived from our customer base as we continue to execute our strategy to expand our reach to serve larger, complex merchants. Non-GAAP net income represents net income adjusted for certain non-cash and other nonrecurring items that management believes are not indicative of ongoing operations, such as amortization of acquired intangible assets, acquisition, restructuring and integration costs, revaluation of contingent liabilities, gain on sale of subsidiaries, impairment of intangible assets, loss on extinguishment of debt, gain (loss) on investments in securities, change in TRA liability, equity-based compensation, and foreign exchange and other nonrecurring items. Adjusted EBITDA is the primary financial performance measure used by management to evaluate its business and monitor results of operations. Adjusted EBITDA represents EBITDA further adjusted for certain non-cash and other nonrecurring items that management believes are not indicative of ongoing operations. These adjustments include acquisition, restructuring and integration costs, revaluation of contingent liabilities, gain on sale of subsidiaries, impairment of intangible assets, loss on extinguishment of debt, gain (loss) on investments in securities, change in TRA liability, equity-based compensation, and foreign exchange and other nonrecurring items. Adjusted EBITDA Margin represents Adjusted EBITDA divided by GRLNF. Free cash flow represents net cash provided by operating activities adjusted for certain non-discretionary capital expenditures. Adjusted Free Cash Flow represents free cash flow further adjusted for certain transactions that are not indicative of future operating cash flows, including acquisition, restructuring and integration costs, other nonrecurring expenses, and nonrecurring strategic capital expenditures that are not indicative of ongoing activities. We believe Adjusted Free Cash Flow is useful to measure the funds generated in a given period that are available to invest in the business, to repurchase stock and to make strategic decisions. The Adjusted EBITDA conversion rate is calculated as Adjusted Free Cash Flow divided by Adjusted EBITDA. We use non-GAAP financial measures to supplement financial information presented on a GAAP basis. We believe that excluding certain items from our GAAP results allows management to better understand our consolidated financial performance and, in the case of Adjusted Free Cash Flow, our liquidity, from period to period and better project our future consolidated financial performance as forecasts are developed at a level of detail different from that used to prepare GAAP-based financial measures. Moreover, we believe these non-GAAP financial measures provide our stakeholders with useful information to help them evaluate our operating results by facilitating an enhanced understanding of our operating performance and, in the case of Adjusted Free Cash Flow, our liquidity, and enabling them to make more meaningful period to period comparisons. There are limitations to the use of the non-GAAP financial measures presented in this letter. Our non-GAAP financial measures may not be comparable to similarly titled measures of other companies. Other companies, including companies in our industry, may calculate non-GAAP financial measures differently than we do, limiting the usefulness of those measures for comparative purposes. The non-GAAP financial measures are not meant to be considered as indicators of performance, or in the case of Adjusted Free Cash Flow, as an indicator of liquidity, in isolation from or as a substitute for financial information prepared in accordance with GAAP, and should be read only in conjunction with financial information presented on a GAAP basis. Reconciliations of EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA, GRLNF, Non-GAAP net income, Non-GAAP EPS, free cash flow and Adjusted Free Cash Flow to, in each case, its most directly comparable GAAP financial measure are presented in Appendix - Financial Information. For 2026, we are unable to provide a reconciliation of GRLNF, Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted Free Cash Flow and Non-GAAP EPS to Gross Profit, Net Income, net cash provided by operating activities, and net income (loss) per Class A and C share, respectively, the nearest comparable GAAP measures, without unreasonable efforts. We encourage you to review the reconciliations in conjunction with the presentation of the non-GAAP financial measures for each of the periods presented. In future fiscal periods, we may exclude such items and may incur income and expenses similar to these excluded items. In addition, key performance indicators include volume, Blended Spread and margin. Volume is defined as the total dollar amount of payments that we deliver for settlement on behalf of our merchants. Included in volume are dollars routed via our international payments platform, alternative payment methods, including cryptocurrency, stored value, gift cards and stock donations, plus volume we route to third party merchant acquirers on behalf of strategic enterprise merchant relationships. We do maintain transaction processing on certain legacy platforms that are not defined as volume. Blended Spread represents the average yield Shift4 earns on the average volume processed for a given period after network fees. Blended Spread is calculated as payments-based revenue less gateway revenue and network fees for a given period divided by the volume processed for the same period. November 5, 2026 Dear Fellow Shareholders, 2026 has thus far been a painful year for shareholders. Our share price is down roughly 40% since the beginning of the year, and skepticism remains high for both our company and the sector more broadly. As a group, employees and our founder own over 40% of the company. We share your pain and sincerely appreciate the confidence our long-term shareholders have in the business. I can speculate on the efficiency of markets and the broader environment, but the more productive exercise is to focus on our business performance, its evolution over time and why our story is so misunderstood at times. To that end, we clearly have work to do. I believe this quarter and year as a whole will serve as proof points of the durability of our business, our ability to allocate capital for diversified growth, and the power of our products; that are category leaders across multiple attractive verticals and continue to win. We can also make the story easier to understand and our strategy more predictable to our investors. Durability: During the quarter we largely achieved our guidance despite what I would categorize as a more challenging backdrop than we’ve seen in recent years. Travel disruption continues to weigh on our Tax-Free Shopping business, and same store sales continued to face pressure off reasonably low comparables. Despite this: • Gross revenue was $1.3 billion, up 12% year over year; Gross revenue less network fees were $648 million and gross profit was $434 million, up 10% (or 9% on an organic constant currency basis) and 6% year over year, respectively. • Payments based revenue less network fees, our north star, grew 18% in the quarter and 23% year to date. • Net income was $40 million for the quarter. EBITDA was $261 million and Adjusted EBITDA was $310 million. Each was up 13% and 6% respectively. • Lastly, net cash from operating activities was $221 million and Adjusted Free Cash Flow was $200 million, a quarterly record. While we continue to feel the impact of both travel disruptions, which has been more pronounced in the fourth quarter, and weaker same store sales, we are growing despite them. I believe these headwinds will abate in the times ahead. Capital Allocation: Our free cash flow affords us the ability to invest in multiple avenues of growth while also returning capital to shareholders in the form of stock repurchases. During the quarter we invested record amounts in product development and expanded into multiple new country markets, we repurchased roughly 5% of shares outstanding and made progress towards an exciting M&A transaction that will both expand our capabilities and bring us attractive customers at reasonable cost. Each of these areas of investment will continue to drive earnings per share growth. Products that Win: This quarter we signed Kahala Brands, now our single largest restaurant customer, added the MSG Sphere and several EU hotels, and won Kering, one of the largest luxury groups in the world, whose brands include Gucci, for tax-free shopping. Our experience handling the most demanding consumer experiences and product suite designed for “in real life” engagement is why such amazing customers trust Shift4. Handling the World Cup, or World Series for that matter, gives our merchants the confidence needed to choose Shift4. The Road Ahead: We continue to see opportunities to trade single product revenue for higher quality payments-based revenues and will do that as aggressively as we can. Our international expansion remains on track but can also improve from here. We are live in 15 countries with Shift4 One ahead of schedule and expect to be exiting the year with nearly $50M in synergies from Global Blue, which puts us well on our way to our previously stated 2027 synergy target of $70M. As mentioned previously, this performance is not without room for criticism. Travel disruptions, currency fluctuation, inflation, and same-store sales have all created tangible headwinds for the business. We are revising our full year 2026 Volume guidance to $240 to $250 billion, tightening the upper end of the range, lowering our full-year 2026 Gross Revenue less Network Fees guidance to $2.45 to $2.46 billion, and adjusting full-year Adjusted EBITDA to $1.11 to $1.13 billion. Despite these downward revisions, we are also affirming Adjusted Free Cash Flow of $465 to $475 million. For those keeping score, this guidance is roughly 4% lower on Gross Revenues Less Network Fees and 6% lower on Adjusted EBITDA than our original full year 2026 guidance. Free Cash Flow conversion is unchanged at 42%. We believe these revisions reflect both an acknowledgement of continued macro challenges and also near-term opportunities to accelerate payments-based revenue growth in the quarters ahead. Since our IPO we have grown our revenues by 35% annually, diversified across multiple industry verticals and dozens of geographies, improved EBITDA margins by 55%, and equity dilution of just 9%.
